findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "voidly_incident_detail" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use this when you have a published Voidly incident ID (for example IR-2026-0253, from a Voidly page, report or citation) and need that censorship or shutdown in…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: voidly_measurement_summary · Private data: voidly_incident_stats · Public sink: voidly_country_data.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: voidly_measurement_summary · Private data: voidly_incident_stats · Public sink: voidly_country_data

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "voidly_incident_stats" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Read aggregate public incident counts. findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
